data.reasoning: The disagreement stems from a tool error (HTTP 400 API failure) in the qwen report, not genuine security concerns. The deepseek report successfully reviewed all files and found standard AUR packaging: a pinned GitHub release tarball with SHA256 checksum, static variable definitions, and no executable code in global scope. The qwen report's initial PKGBUILD audit (before the error) also found no dangerous top-level code. No injection patterns, obfuscated commands, or unexpected network operations were detected.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model encountered an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) during full PKGBUILD review, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. However, its initial PKGBUILD audit passed successfully, finding no dangerous top-level code. The deepseek model completed the full review without errors and found the package safe. This is a tool failure, not a security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to API error (HTTP 400)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should be distinguished from genuine security disagreements when determining verdict
Initial audit results can provide useful signal even when full audits fail due to tool errors
When one model encounters a tool error and another completes successfully with consistent findings, the successful report should carry the verdict
